newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Insurance Dept to investigate American Intl.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Insurance Dept to investigate American Intl.

text.p: California's Department of Insurance on Friday said it would investigate American International Group Inc's business practices in the state.
The Insurance Department said the investigation would be launched because "concerns have mounted regarding AIG's conduct following its losing bid in the Golden Eagle insolvency proceedings."
Golden Eagle Insurance Co was seized by the Department of Insurance in January after investigators allegedly turned up evidence the company had manipulated its financial records.
AIG had been expected to take over the company. But on May 30 Liberty Mutual Group beat out AIG in a court-supervised auction to acquire Golden Eagle.
AIG has appealed the decision, arguing that it should have won the bidding for the company.
In a statement Friday, the Department of Insurance accused AIG of attempting to disrupt the "economic relations" between Golden Eagle and its new owner, Liberty Mutual.
The department alleged that AIG was spreading false information to third parties in an effort to create "anxiety and start problems" for the new Golden Eagle.

"We have received numerous complaints from consumers about the company's conduct and this, together with the recent disturbing events in the Golden Eagle rehabilitation, raise serious questions that require answers from this company," said Joel Laucher, the Department of Insurance's division chief of consumer services.

The department said a hearing would be held in the coming weeks to review the allegations. "The hearing will necessarily require the subpoena of witnesses, including officers, directors and agents of the company," the department said.
AIG was not immediately available to comment.
